name: NA49
notes: NA49 is the second experiment of the H2 heavy-ion family (NA35, NA49, NA61/SHINE); NA61/SHINE inherited its detector (recorded on experiment:na61-shine as predecessor).

Placed in EHN1 inferred from the H2 beam line (NA61/SHINE inherited the apparatus and its Beams page names Experimental Hall North 1); no fetched source states the hall for NA49 directly, so the placement confidence is uncertain.
No collaboration website was reachable (na49info.web.cern.ch requires a CERN login) and the NA49 detector paper (NIM A430 (1999) 210) is not on arXiv, so no specs are recorded.
INSPIRE experiment id not looked up: inspirehep.net is off-limits to coverage streams (STREAM_RULES); external.inspire_experiment left null for the integrator.

physics_goals.value: Search for the quark-gluon plasma and its onset in lead-lead collisions as a function of collision energy

summary.plain: NA49 was a large detector at CERN's SPS that recorded lead-lead and other collisions to look for the transition to quark-gluon plasma. Its energy scan found sudden changes in particle production near 30 GeV per nucleon, evidence for where plasma formation starts.
summary.technical: NA49: large-acceptance hadron spectrometer on the H2 beam line of the CERN North Area (four large-volume TPCs, two in superconducting dipole magnets) studying Pb+Pb and other collisions at 20A-158A GeV (event-by-event fluctuations in 1994-1997, energy scan 1998-2002); discovered the onset of deconfinement signatures (the K+/pi+ horn, step and kink); its detector passed to NA61/SHINE.
